units.literal: Eight commanderies and principalities had great floods.

units.zh: 冬十一月壬子，以隴西王泰都督關中諸軍事。
units.en: Renzi: Sima Tai took command of Guanzhong.
units.literal: On the day renzi of winter, eleventh month, king Tai of Longxi was appointed supervisor of all military affairs within the passes.

units.zh: 十二月，遣侍御史巡遭水諸郡。
units.en: Twelfth month: investigating censors were sent to tour commanderies that had suffered flood.
units.literal: In the twelfth month investigating censors were dispatched to tour commanderies that had suffered flood.

units.zh: 出後宮才人、妓女以下二百七十人歸于家。
units.en: Two hundred seventy palace women of lower rank were sent home.
units.literal: Two hundred seventy women from talented ladies and singing-girls downward in the rear palace were sent home.

units.zh: 始制大臣聽終喪三年。
units.en: For the first time chief ministers could sit the full three-year parent funeral.
units.literal: It was first decreed that great ministers might observe the full three-year mourning for parents.

units.zh: 己亥，河陰雨赤雪二頃。
units.en: Jihai: red snow covered two qing at Heyin.
units.literal: On the day jihai crimson snow fell for two qing in Heyin.

units.zh: 是歲，扶南等二十一國、馬韓等十一國遣使來獻。
units.en: Twenty-one southern and eleven Korean-style states sent embassies.
units.literal: That year twenty-one states including Funan and eleven including Ma Han sent envoys to present tribute.

units.zh: 八年春正月戊申朔，日有蝕之。
units.en: Taikang 8, wushen: eclipse.
units.literal: In the eighth year, spring, first month, on the first day wushen, there was an eclipse of the sun.

units.zh: 太廟殿陷。
units.en: The great temple’s main hall fell in.
units.literal: The hall of the grand ancestral temple collapsed inward.

units.zh: 三月乙丑，臨商觀震。
units.en: Third month, yichou: the Shangguan watchtower rocked in a tremor.
units.literal: On the day yichou of the third month the Shangguan observation tower was shaken by an earthquake.

units.zh: 夏四月，齊國、天水隕霜，傷麥。
units.en: Summer frost [37] ruined wheat in Qi and Tianshui.
units.literal: In summer, the fourth month, Qi principality and Tianshui had killing frost [37] that injured the wheat.

units.zh: 六月，魯國大風，拔樹木，壞百姓廬舍。
units.en: In the sixth month, great winds in Lu principality uprooted trees and damaged the huts and houses of the common people.
units.literal: In the sixth month Lu principality had great wind that uprooted trees and ruined commoners’ huts.

units.zh: 郡國八大水。
units.en: Eight provinces flooded again.
units.literal: Eight commanderies and principalities had great floods.

units.zh: 秋七月，前殿地陷，深數丈，中有破船。
units.en: The front hall yard opened into a pit revealing an ancient wreck.
units.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, the ground before the front hall collapsed several zhang deep, and within was a broken boat.

units.zh: 八月，東夷二國內附。
units.en: Two more Yi groups enrolled.
units.literal: In the eighth month two states of the eastern Yi submitted within the borders.

units.zh: 九月，改營太廟。
units.en: Ninth month: plans to rebuild the ancestral temple.
units.literal: In the ninth month the grand temple was ordered rebuilt.

units.zh: 冬十月，南康平固縣吏李豐反，聚眾攻郡縣，自號將軍。
units.en: Winter, tenth month: Li Feng, a clerk of Pinggu county in Nankang, rebelled, gathered a crowd, attacked the commanderies and counties, and styled himself general.
units.literal: In winter, the tenth month clerk Li Feng of Pinggu county in Nankang rebelled, gathered a crowd, attacked commanderies and counties, and styled himself general.

units.zh: 十一月，海安令蕭輔聚眾反。
units.en: Eleventh month: Xiao Fu rose at Hai’an.
units.literal: In the eleventh month Xiao Fu, magistrate of Hai’an, gathered a crowd and rebelled.

units.zh: 十二月，吳興人蔣迪聚黨反，圍陽羨縣，州郡捕討，皆伏誅。
units.en: Twelfth month: Jiang Di’s band in Wu-xing was wiped out.
units.literal: In the twelfth month Jiang Di of Wu-xing gathered a party, rebelled, besieged Yangxian county, and was hunted down by province and commandery; all were executed.

units.zh: 南夷扶南、西域康居國各遣使來獻。
units.en: Funan and Kangju sent embassies.
units.literal: Funan in the southern Yi and Kangju in the Western Regions each sent envoys to present tribute.

units.zh: 是歲，郡國五地震。
units.en: Five provinces reported quakes.
units.literal: That year five commanderies and principalities suffered earthquakes.

units.zh: 九年春正月壬申朔，日有蝕之。
units.en: Taikang 9, renshen: eclipse.
units.literal: In the ninth year, spring, first month, on the first day renshen, there was an eclipse of the sun.

units.zh: 詔曰：「興化之本，由政平訟理也。
units.en: An edict said, "The root of raising transformation lies in government being even and lawsuits being ordered.
units.literal: An edict said: “The root of promoting transformation lies in even government and balanced lawsuits.

units.zh: 二千石長吏不能勤恤人隱，而輕挾私故，興長刑獄，又多貪濁，煩撓百姓。
units.en: He scolded magistrates who pile up cases for private gain and bleed the people.
units.literal: Governors at two thousand piculs and chiefs who cannot diligently pity the people’s hardships, but lightly indulge private reasons, thereby prolonging litigation, and who moreover are mostly greedy and corrupt, vexing the hundred surnames—

units.zh: 其敕刺史二千石糾其穢濁，舉其公清，有司議其黜陟。
units.en: Inspectors must expose the corrupt and lift the clean for central review.
units.literal: order the inspectors and two-thousand-picul men to impeach their filth, praise their fairness and purity, and let the offices deliberate their demotion or promotion.

units.zh: 令內外群官舉清能，拔寒素。」
units.en: Every office must nominate honest talent from poor families.”
units.literal: Order civil and military officials within and without to recommend the pure and capable and to raise men of cold and humble background.”

units.zh: 江東四郡地震。
units.en: The four commanderies east of the Yangzi suffered an earthquake.
units.literal: There was an earthquake in the four commanderies east of the Yangzi River.

units.zh: 二月，尚書右僕射、陽夏侯胡奮卒，以尚書朱整爲尚書右僕射。
units.en: Second month: Hu Fen, right vice-president and marquis of Yangxia, died; Zhu Zheng, a master of writing, was made right vice-president.
units.literal: In the second month Hu Fen, senior vice-director of the masters of the right and marquis of Yangxia, died; Zhu Zheng of the masters of writing was appointed senior vice-director of the masters of the right.

units.zh: 三月丁丑，皇后親桑于西郊，賜帛各有差。
units.en: Dingchou: the empress held the silkworm rite and gifts followed.
units.literal: On the day dingchou of the third month the empress personally tended silkworms in the western suburb; silks were bestowed each according to difference.

units.zh: 壬辰，初并二社爲一。
units.en: Renchen: the paired earth gods were combined in one rite.
units.literal: On the day renchen the two soil altars were first merged into one.

units.zh: 夏四月，江南郡國八地震；
units.en: Summer: eight south-of-river counties shook;
units.literal: In summer, the fourth month, eight commanderies and principalities south of the Yangzi suffered earthquakes;

units.zh: 隴西隕霜，傷宿麥。
units.en: Longxi frost killed the winter wheat.
units.literal: Longxi had killing frost that injured the winter wheat.

units.zh: 五月，義陽王奇有罪，黜爲三縱亭侯。
units.en: Fifth month: Sima Qi of Yiyang lost his kingship for crime, becoming village marquis of Sanzongting.
units.literal: In the fifth month king Qi of Yiyang committed a crime and was degraded to marquis of Sanzongting.

units.zh: 詔內外群官舉守令之才。
units.en: The court called for nominations of worthy prefects and magistrates.
units.literal: An edict ordered civil and military officials within and without each to recommend men with talent to be shepherds and magistrates.

units.zh: 六月庚子朔，日有蝕之。
units.en: Sixth month, new moon gengzi: eclipse.
units.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, gengzi, there was an eclipse of the sun.

units.zh: 徙章武王威爲義陽王。
units.en: Sima Wei moved from Zhangwu to Yiyang.
units.literal: King Wei of Zhangwu was transferred to be king of Yiyang.

units.zh: 郡國三十二大旱，傷麥。
units.en: Thirty-two provinces baked in drought that withered the wheat crop.
units.literal: Thirty-two commanderies and principalities suffered great drought that injured the wheat.

units.zh: 秋八月壬子，星隕如雨。
units.en: Eighth month, renzi: a meteor shower lit the sky.
units.literal: In autumn, the eighth month, on the day renzi, stars fell like rain.

units.zh: 詔郡國五歲刑以下決遣，無留庶獄。
units.en: He told magistrates to clear dockets of minor sentences and end jail backlog.
units.literal: An edict ordered commanderies and principalities to dispose of penal cases up to five years’ labor and not to leave common lawsuits detained.

units.zh: 九月，東夷七國詣校尉內附。
units.en: Seven Yi peoples reported to the frontier colonel and enrolled as subjects.
units.literal: In the ninth month seven states of the eastern Yi came to the colonel and submitted within the borders.

units.zh: 郡國二十四螟。
units.en: Crop-worms blighted twenty-four provinces.
units.literal: Twenty-four commanderies and principalities suffered from grain-eating caterpillars.

units.zh: 冬十二月癸卯，立河間平王洪子英爲章武王。
units.en: Guimao: Ying, son of Hejian’s Prince Hong, became king of Zhangwu.
units.literal: On the day guimao of winter, twelfth month, Ying, son of king Hong the peaceful of Hejian, was established as king of Zhangwu.

units.zh: 戊申，青龍、黃龍各一見于魯國。
units.en: Wushen: one blue and one yellow dragon sighted in Lu.
units.literal: On the day wushen an azure dragon and a yellow dragon were each seen in Lu principality.

units.zh: 十年夏四月，以京兆太守劉霄、陽平太守梁柳有政績，各賜穀千斛。
units.en: Taikang 10, summer, fourth month: Liu Xiao, prefect of Jingzhao, and Liang Liu, prefect of Yangping, were each granted a thousand hu of grain for their administration.
units.literal: In summer, the fourth month of the tenth year, because Jingzhao prefect Liu Xiao and Yangping prefect Liang Liu had administrative achievements, each was granted one thousand hu of grain.

units.zh: 郡國八隕霜。
units.en: Black frost struck eight provinces.
units.literal: Eight commanderies and principalities had killing frost.

units.zh: 太廟成。
units.en: The new imperial temple stood finished.
units.literal: The grand ancestral temple was completed.

units.zh: 乙巳，遷神主于新廟，帝迎于道左，遂祫祭。
units.en: Yisi: ancestral tablets entered the new shrine in a procession the emperor met in person, followed by a combined offering.
units.literal: On the day yisi the spirit tablets were moved to the new temple; the emperor welcomed them on the left of the road, then performed the joint sacrifice.

units.zh: 大赦，文武增位一等，作廟者二等。
units.en: Amnesty came with promotions—one step for officials, two for temple builders.
units.literal: A great amnesty was declared; civil and military officials were advanced one grade in rank, and those who built the temple two grades.

units.zh: 丁未，尚書右僕射、廣興侯朱整卒。
units.en: Dingwei: Zhu Zheng died.
units.literal: On the day dingwei Zhu Zheng, senior vice-director of the masters of the right and marquis of Guangxing, died.

units.zh: 癸丑，崇賢殿災。
units.en: Guichou: fire consumed the Chongxian hall.
units.literal: On the day guichou the Chongxian hall caught fire.

units.zh: 五月，鮮卑慕容廆來降，東夷十一國內附。
units.en: Fifth month: Murong Hui yielded while eleven Yi realms joined Jin.
units.literal: In the fifth month Murong Hui of the Xianbei came to surrender, and eleven states of the eastern Yi submitted within the borders.

units.zh: 六月庚子，山陽公劉瑾薨。
units.en: Gengzi of the sixth month: Liu Jin, duke of Shanyang, died.
units.literal: On the day gengzi of the sixth month Liu Jin, mountain-yang duke, died.

units.zh: 復置二社。
units.en: The paired earth-god altars were reinstated.
units.literal: The two soil altars were restored.

units.zh: 冬十月壬子，徙南宮王承爲武邑王。
units.en: Renzi: the southern-palace king became prince of Wuyi.
units.literal: On the day renzi of winter, tenth month, king Cheng of the southern palace was transferred to be king of Wuyi.

units.zh: 十一月丙辰，守尚書令、左光祿大夫荀勖卒。
units.en: Bingchen: Xun Xu died in office.
units.literal: On the day bingchen of the eleventh month Xun Xu, acting supervisor of the masters of writing and grand master for splendid happiness on the left, died.

units.zh: 帝疾瘳，賜王公以下帛有差。
units.en: On partial recovery he handed out graded silk to the nobility.
units.literal: When the emperor’s illness abated, silks were bestowed on the kings and dukes downward, each according to difference.

units.zh: 含章殿鞠室火。
units.en: Fire broke out in the Hanzhang hall’s indoor ball court.
units.literal: The ball-court chamber in the Hanzhang hall caught fire.

units.zh: 甲申，以汝南王亮爲大司馬、大都督、假黃鉞。
units.en: Jiashen: Sima Liang became grand marshal and supreme commander with the yellow axe.
units.literal: On the day jiashen Sima Liang, king of Runan, was appointed grand marshal, supreme commander, and given the yellow axe as credential.

units.zh: 改封南陽王柬爲秦王，始平王瑋爲楚王，濮陽王允爲淮南王，並假節之國，各統方州軍事。
units.en: Three princes were sent out with full powers—Jian to Qin, Wei to Chu, Yun to Huainan.
units.literal: King Jian of Nanyang was transferred to be king of Qin, king Wei of Shiping to king of Chu, king Yun of Puyang to king of Huainan, each bearing the staff of authority to his state and commanding regional military affairs.

units.zh: 立皇子乂爲長沙王，穎爲成都王，晏爲吳王，熾爲豫章王，演爲代王，皇孫遹爲廣陵王。
units.en: He established the imperial son Yi as King of Changsha, Ying as King of Chengdu, Yan as King of Wu, Chi as King of Yuzhang, Yan as King of Dai, and the imperial grandson Yu as King of Guangling.
units.literal: He established the imperial son Yi as king of Changsha, Ying as king of Chengdu, Yan as king of Wu, Chi as king of Yuzhang, Yan as king of Dai, and the imperial grandson Yu as king of Guangling.

units.zh: 立濮陽王子迪爲漢王，始平王子儀爲毗陵王，汝南王次子羕爲西陽公。
units.en: He established Di, son of the King of Puyang, as King of Han; Yi, son of the King of Shiping, as King of Piling; and Yang, second son of the King of Runan, as Duke of Xiyang.
units.literal: He established Di, son of the king of Puyang, as king of Han; Yi, son of the king of Shiping, as king of Piling; Yang, second son of the king of Runan, as duke of Xiyang.

units.zh: 徙扶風王暢爲順陽王，暢弟歆爲新野公，琅邪王覲弟澹爲東武公，繇爲東安公，漼爲廣陵公，卷爲東莞公。
units.en: He transferred Chang, King of Fufeng, to be King of Shunyang; made Xin, Chang’s younger brother, Duke of Xinye; and made Dan, younger brother of Jin, King of Langye, Duke of Dongwu, You Duke of Dong’an, Cui Duke of Guangling, and Juan Duke of Dongguan.
units.literal: King Chang of Fufeng was transferred to be king of Shunyang; Xin, Chang’s younger brother, was made duke of Xinye; Dan, younger brother of king Jin of Langye, duke of Dongwu; You duke of Dong’an; Cui duke of Guangling; Juan duke of Dongguan.

units.zh: 改諸王國相爲內史。
units.en: Princely “chancellors” became “interior historians.”
units.literal: The ministers of princely states were renamed interior historians.

units.zh: 十二月庚寅，太廟梁折。
units.en: Gengyin [39]: a roof-beam cracked in the ancestral temple.
units.literal: On the day gengyin of the twelfth month [39] a beam in the grand temple broke.

units.zh: 是歲，東夷絕遠三十餘國、西南夷二十餘國來獻。
units.en: Embassies arrived from thirty-plus eastern and twenty-plus southwestern tribes.
units.literal: That year more than thirty distant eastern Yi states and more than twenty southwestern Yi states came to present tribute.

units.zh: 虜奚軻男女十萬口來降。
units.en: A hundred thousand Xike tribespeople submitted to Jin.
units.literal: One hundred thousand persons, men and women, of the Xike tribe came to surrender.

units.zh: 太熙元年春正月辛酉朔，改元。
units.en: In Taixi 1, spring, first month, on the xinyou new moon, the reign title was changed.
units.literal: In Taixi 1, spring, first month, on the xinyou new moon, the reign period was changed.

units.zh: 己巳，以尚書左僕射王渾爲司徒，司空衛瓘爲太保。
units.en: On jisi, Wang Hun was promoted from Left Supervisor of the Secretariat to Minister over the Masses, and Wei Guan from Minister of Works to Grand Protector.
units.literal: On jisi, Wang Hun, Left Supervisor of the Secretariat, was made Minister over the Masses, and Wei Guan, Minister of Works, was made Grand Protector.

units.en: Manuscripts mark editorial note [40] here.
units.literal: [40] The received text carries commentary marker [40] at this point.

units.zh: 二月辛丑，東夷七國朝貢。
units.en: Second month, xinchou: seven Yi missions at court.
units.literal: On the day xinchou of the second month seven eastern Yi states came to court with tribute.

units.zh: 琅邪王覲薨。
units.en: The king of Langye, Sima Jin, died.
units.literal: King Jin of Langye died.

units.zh: 三月甲子，以右光祿大夫石鑒爲司空。
units.en: Jiazi: Shi Jian became minister of works.
units.literal: On the day jiazi of the third month Shi Jian, grand master for splendid happiness on the right, was appointed minister of works.

units.zh: 夏四月辛丑，以侍中車騎將軍楊駿爲太尉、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事。
units.en: Xinchou: Yang Jun took the triple portfolio—grand commandant, commander-in-chief, and chief of the secretariat.
units.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the day xinchou, Yang Jun, palace attendant and general of chariots and cavalry, was appointed grand commandant, supervisor of all military affairs within and without, and recorder of masters-of-writing business.

units.zh: 己酉，帝崩于含章殿，時年五十五，葬峻陽陵，廟號世祖。
units.en: Jiyou: the emperor expired in Hanzhang at fifty-five, buried at the Junyang tomb with the temple name Shizu.
units.literal: On the day jiyou the emperor died in the Hanzhang hall at age fifty-five; he was buried at Junyang mausoleum with temple name Shizu.

units.zh: 帝宇量弘厚，造次必於仁恕；
units.en: He was large-spirited and humane even under pressure.
units.literal: The emperor’s bearing was broad and his capacity magnanimous; even in haste he acted with benevolence and forgiveness.

units.zh: 容納讜正，未嘗失色於人；
units.en: He heard hard truths without losing his temper.
units.literal: He accepted blunt counsel and never showed anger on his face toward others.

units.zh: 明達善謀，能斷大事，故得撫寧萬國，綏靜四方。
units.en: His judgment pacified the realm.
units.literal: He was perspicacious, skilled in planning, and able to decide great matters, and therefore could soothe and stabilize the myriad regions and bring quiet to the four quarters.

units.zh: 承魏氏奢侈刻弊之後，百姓思古之遺風，乃厲以恭儉，敦以寡慾。
units.en: After Wei’s luxury and cruelty, he modeled austerity and restraint.
units.literal: Following the Wei dynasty’s extravagance and harsh exactions, the hundred surnames longed for the surviving air of antiquity; he therefore enforced reverence and frugality and pressed for few desires.

units.zh: 有司嘗奏御牛青絲紖斷，詔以青麻代之。
units.en: When clerks noted the palace ox’s silk lead had broken, he told them to use hemp instead.
units.literal: Once the offices memorialized that the imperial ox’s blue silk halter had snapped; he ordered hemp substituted.

units.zh: 臨朝寬裕，法度有恆。
units.en: His sessions were calm and the code steady.
units.literal: In court he was lenient and law and measure remained constant.

units.zh: 高陽許允既爲文帝所殺，允子奇爲太常丞。
units.en: Xu Yun, whom Wen had executed, left a son Qi in the ritual office.
units.literal: Xu Yun of Gaoyang had already been killed by emperor Wen; Yun’s son Qi served as assistant director of the grand master of ceremonies.

units.zh: 帝將有事於太廟，朝議以奇受害之門，不欲接近左右，請出爲長史。
units.en: Ministers wanted Qi barred from the rite as a victim’s son.
units.literal: When the emperor was about to perform business in the grand temple, court discussion held that Qi came from a house that had suffered harm and should not be kept near the throne, requesting he be sent out as senior clerk.

units.zh: 帝乃追述允夙望，稱奇之才，擢爲祠部郎，時論稱其夷曠。
units.en: The emperor overruled them, praised Qi, and raised him—critics called it magnanimous.
units.literal: The emperor then recalled Xu Yun’s old repute, praised Qi’s talent, promoted him to director in the sacrifices bureau, and opinion of the time praised his fairness and breadth.

units.zh: 平吳之後，天下乂安，遂怠於政術，耽於遊宴，寵愛后黨，親貴當權，舊臣不得專任，彝章紊廢，請謁行矣。
units.en: Peace bred complacency: harem kin and favorites took the reins while law grew slack.
units.literal: After Wu was pacified, all under heaven was at peace; thereupon he slackened in governing methods, indulged in roaming feasts, doted on the empress’s kin, let close nobles hold power, no longer gave old ministers sole responsibility, canonical regulations fell into disorder, and soliciting favor became the way.

units.zh: 爰至末年，知惠帝弗克負荷，然恃皇孫聰睿，故無廢立之心。
units.en: Late in life he saw Hui’s weakness but pinned hope on a bright grandson.
units.literal: By his last years he knew that emperor Hui could not bear the burden, yet he trusted in the imperial grandson’s cleverness and therefore had no mind to change the heir.

units.zh: 復慮非賈后所生，終致危敗，遂與腹心共圖後事。
units.en: He worried Jia’s lack of maternity would doom the line and schemed with confidants.
units.literal: He again feared that because the child was not born of empress Jia, disaster would ultimately follow, and therefore plotted the aftermath with his intimates.

units.zh: 說者紛然，久而不定，竟用王佑之謀，遣太子母弟秦王柬都督關中，楚王瑋、淮南王允並鎮守要害，以強帝室。
units.en: Opinions were confused and remained unsettled for a long time. In the end, he adopted Wang You’s plan, sending Jian, King of Qin and the crown prince’s younger full brother, to command Guanzhong, while Wei, King of Chu, and Yun, King of Huainan, both guarded strategic points in order to strengthen the imperial house.
units.literal: Opinions flew thick and long without settlement; in the end he adopted Wang You’s plan, sending the crown prince’s younger uterine brother, king Jian of Qin, to command Guanzhong, while kings Wei of Chu and Yun of Huainan jointly guarded critical points to strengthen the imperial house.

units.zh: 又恐楊氏之偪，復以佑爲北軍中候，以典禁兵。
units.en: To check the Yangs he gave Wang You the northern-army baton.
units.literal: Fearing pressure from the Yang clan, he again made Wang You inspector of the northern armies to command the palace guard.

units.zh: 既而寢疾彌留，至於大漸，佐命元勳，皆已先沒，群臣惶惑，計無所從。
units.en: When death neared, his great generals were gone and the court panicked.
units.literal: Soon he lay gravely ill; as he approached the final crisis, the founding ministers had all predeceased him, and the host of officials were frightened and at a loss.

units.zh: 會帝小差，有詔以汝南王亮輔政，又欲令朝士之有名望年少者數人佐之，楊駿祕而不宣。
units.en: A brief rally produced orders for Sima Liang and young worthies—Yang Jun hid the edict.
units.literal: When the emperor briefly improved, an edict ordered king Liang of Runan to assist the government, and he also wished to have several young courtiers of high repute assist him, but Yang Jun suppressed the edict and did not proclaim it.

units.zh: 帝復尋至迷亂，楊后輒爲詔以駿輔政，促亮進發。
units.en: Empress Yang forged a regency for Yang Jun.
units.literal: The emperor relapsed into confusion; empress Yang then forged an edict making Yang Jun regent and urging Liang to hurry to the capital.

units.zh: 帝尋小間，問汝南王來未，意欲見之，有所付託。
units.en: In a lucid moment he asked for Sima Liang.
units.literal: The emperor briefly cleared and asked whether the king of Runan had arrived, intending to see him and entrust something.

units.zh: 左右答言未至，帝遂困篤。
units.en: Told Liang had not come, he sank back into coma.
units.literal: Those at his side answered that he had not yet arrived, and the emperor thereupon sank into critical illness.

units.zh: 中朝之亂，實始於斯矣。
units.en: The mid-realm disasters trace to this bedside failure.
units.literal: The turmoil at court truly began from this.

units.zh: 制曰：武皇承基，誕膺天命，握圖御宇，敷化導民，以佚代勞，以治易亂。
units.en: The court’s summation runs thus: Emperor Wu inherited the enterprise, claimed Heaven’s charge, mastered the realm’s map, and turned exhaustion and disorder into rest and rule.
units.literal: The official rescript states: The Martial Emperor received the foundation, truly bore heaven’s mandate, grasped the chart and ruled the realm, spread transformation and guided the people, replacing toil with ease and exchanging chaos for order.

units.zh: 絕縑綸之貢，去雕琢之飾，制奢俗以變儉約，止澆風而反淳朴。
units.en: He banned luxury tribute and chased the court back toward plain living.
units.literal: He cut off the tribute of fine silks, removed carved and polished ornament, curbed extravagant custom toward frugality, and checked dissolute winds to return to simplicity.

units.zh: 雅好直言，留心采擢，劉毅、裴楷以質直見容，嵇紹、許奇雖仇讎不棄。
units.en: He welcomed Liu Yi, Pei Kai, Ji Shao, and Xu Qi despite awkward pedigrees.
units.literal: He loved straight words and attended to selection; Liu Yi and Pei Kai were tolerated for blunt honesty, Ji Shao and Xu Qi were not cast aside though they were sons of enemies.

units.zh: 仁以御物，寬而得眾，宏略大度，有帝王之量焉。
units.en: He ruled with humane breadth worthy of a founder.
units.literal: With kindness he governed things, with leniency he won the multitude; he had grand strategy and large tolerance—the measure of a true emperor.

units.zh: 於時民和俗靜，家給人足，聿修武用，思啟封疆。
units.en: The realm prospered while he sharpened the sword for expansion.
units.literal: At that time the people were harmonious and customs quiet, households had enough and persons sufficed; he repaired military readiness and thought to open the frontiers.

units.zh: 決神算於深衷，斷雄圖於議表。
units.en: He decided great strategy in council and in his own mind.
units.literal: He settled divine calculations in his secret heart and cut heroic plans from memorial debate.

units.zh: 馬隆西伐，王濬南征，師不延時，獯虜削跡，兵無血刃，揚越爲墟。
units.en: Ma Long and Wang Jun finished the frontier and the south without prolonged war.
units.literal: Ma Long campaigned west; Wang Jun marched south—the armies did not tarry, the savage tribes were erased, blades scarcely drew blood, and Yang and Yue became wastes.

units.zh: 通上代之不通，服前王之未服。
units.en: He finished what past dynasties could not.
units.literal: He opened what former ages could not open and submitted what former kings had not submitted.

units.zh: 禎祥顯應，風教肅清，天人之功成矣，霸王之業大矣。
units.en: Omens and morale alike proclaimed a golden age.
units.literal: Auspicious omens responded clearly, wind and instruction were sternly pure; the merit of heaven and man was achieved, the enterprise of hegemon-king was great.

units.zh: 雖登封之禮，讓而不爲，驕泰之心，因斯以起。
units.en: He modestly skipped the Feng sacrifice yet grew complacent.
units.literal: Although he yielded and did not perform the Mount Tai enfeoffment rite, a mind of pride and ease arose from this.

units.zh: 見土地之廣，謂萬葉而無虞；
units.en: He mistook vast territory for perpetual safety;
units.literal: Seeing the breadth of the land, he supposed myriad generations would need no caution;

units.zh: 睹天下之安，謂千年而永治。
units.en: he mistook quiet rule for an eternal guarantee.
units.literal: beholding the peace of the realm, he thought a thousand years of good order assured.

units.zh: 不知處廣以思狹，則廣可長廣；
units.en: Breadth lasts only if one remembers how easily it narrows;
units.literal: He did not know that dwelling in breadth while thinking of narrow straits can keep breadth long broad;

units.zh: 居治而忘危，則治無常治。
units.en: peace lasts only if peril stays in mind.
units.literal: that sitting in order while forgetting peril means order is not constant order.

units.zh: 加之建立非所，委寄失才，志欲就於升平，行先迎於禍亂。
units.en: Wrong heirs and wrong ministers turned pursuit of stability into invitation to chaos.
units.literal: Add to this that establishment was not in the right place, commissions missed the right men—his aim sought rising peace, yet his acts first invited calamity.

units.zh: 是猶將適越者指沙漠以遵途，欲登山者涉舟航而覓路，所趣逾遠，所尚轉難，南北倍殊，高下相反，求其至也，不亦難乎！
units.en: His choices were as absurd as sailing to a mountaintop.
units.literal: It is like one who would go to Yue pointing at the desert for a road, or one who would climb a mountain crossing by boat to seek a path—the goal grows farther, the object harder, south and north doubly wrong, high and low reversed; to seek arrival—is it not hard!

units.zh: 況以新集易動之基，而無久安難拔之慮，故賈充凶豎，懷姦志以擁權；
units.en: On shaky foundations Jia Chong hoarded authority;
units.literal: Moreover, on a newly gathered, easily shaken base, without long-term plans against stubborn peril, therefore Jia Chong, a vicious fellow, harbored treachery and clutched power;

units.zh: 楊駿豺狼，苞禍心以專輔。
units.en: Yang Jun seized the regency with predatory intent.
units.literal: Yang Jun, a jackal-wolf, wrapped a baleful heart and monopolized assistance.

units.zh: 及乎宮車晚出，諒闇未周，藩翰變親以成疏，連兵競滅其本；
units.en: Before the tomb closed, princely armies turned on one another;
units.literal: When at last the palace coach departed late and the mourning curtains had not yet completed their round, the screen princes turned kin into strangers and linked armies to destroy their own root;

units.zh: 棟梁回忠而起僞，擁眾各舉其威。
units.en: Former pillars of state feigned loyalty while raising private armies.
units.literal: beams and pillars turned loyalty into treachery and each raised hosts to vaunt his might.

units.zh: 曾未數年，綱紀大亂，海內版蕩，宗廟播遷。
units.en: Within years the realm shattered and the altars fled.
units.literal: In not a few years the great net was wildly tangled, the seas within the passes were in turmoil, and the ancestral temples were driven to flight.

units.zh: 帝道王猷，反居文身之俗；
units.en: Civilization collapsed into barbarous custom;
units.literal: Imperial way and kingly norm fell among folk who tattoo their bodies;

units.zh: 神州赤縣，翻成被髮之鄉。
units.en: the heartland became a steppe frontier.
units.literal: the divine land of red counties overturned into a realm of disheveled hair.

units.zh: 棄所大以資人，掩其小而自託，爲天下笑，其故何哉﹖良由失慎於前，所以貽患於後。
units.en: He gave away the store and became history’s cautionary tale.
units.literal: He cast aside what was great to enrich others, covered what was small and trusted to it—was he not laughed at by the world? The reason is truly that losing caution earlier planted calamity later.

units.zh: 且知子者賢父，知臣者明君；
units.en: The wise father knows his son, the wise ruler his minister;
units.literal: Moreover, he who knows a son is a worthy father; he who knows a minister is an enlightened lord.

units.zh: 子不肖則家亡，臣不忠則國亂；
units.en: Bad sons ruin families, disloyal ministers ruin states;
units.literal: If a son is not worthy the house perishes; if a minister is not loyal the state is in chaos.

units.zh: 國亂不可以安也，家亡不可以全也。
units.en: Neither state nor house survives that rot.
units.literal: A state in chaos cannot be made tranquil; a house perishing cannot be kept whole.

units.zh: 是以君子防其始，聖人閑其端。
units.en: The wise seal trouble at the source.
units.literal: Therefore the gentleman guards the beginning, the sage blocks the opening.

units.zh: 而世祖惑荀勖之姦謀，迷王渾之僞策，心屢移於眾口，事不定於己圖。
units.en: Shizu listened to Xun Xu and Wang Hun and let rumor steer him.
units.literal: Yet Shizu was deluded by Xun Xu’s treacherous counsel, misled by Wang Hun’s false strategy, his heart repeatedly swayed by many mouths, affairs unsettled by his own deliberation.

units.zh: 元海當除而不除，卒令擾亂區夏；
units.en: He spared Liu Yuan and reaped rebellion;
units.literal: Yuanhai ought to have been removed and was not removed, ultimately letting him disturb the central plain;

units.zh: 惠帝可廢而不廢，終使傾覆洪基。
units.en: He kept a feeble heir and lost the dynasty.
units.literal: Emperor Hui could have been deposed and was not deposed, finally overturning the great foundation.

units.zh: 夫全一人者德之輕，拯天下者功之重，棄一子者忍之小，安社稷者孝之大；
units.en: Saving the state outweighs sparing one prince;
units.literal: To preserve one man is a small virtue; to save the realm is a weighty merit; to cast off one child is a small hardness; to secure the altars is the great filial piety.

units.zh: 況乎資三世而成業，延二孽以喪之，所謂取輕德而捨重功，畏小忍而忘大孝。
units.en: to waste three reigns’ work for two poisonous branches was to pick the lesser good.
units.literal: How much more when he had completed an enterprise through three reigns yet prolonged two baleful shoots to destroy it—what is called taking light virtue and discarding heavy merit, fearing small hardness and forgetting great filial piety.

units.zh: 聖賢之道，豈若斯乎！
units.en: That is not the way of the sages.
units.literal: Can the way of sages and worthies be like this!

units.zh: 雖則善始於初，而乖令終於末，所以殷勤史策，不能無慷慨焉。
units.en: A splendid start and a ruinous end invite the historian’s regret.
units.literal: Although he had a good beginning at first, he missed a fitting end at the last; therefore the histories linger here and must sigh.

units.zh: 校勘記
units.en: Textual notes
units.literal: Collation notes

units.zh: 子文爲沛王 李校：「宗室傳言沛王景字子文。
units.en: For Ziwen as Prince of Pei, Li’s collation note says, "The Biographies of the Imperial Clan says that Prince Jing of Pei had the courtesy name Ziwen.
units.literal: Regarding “Ziwen as king of Pei,” Li’s note: “The house-of-imperial-kin biography says the prince of Pei was named Jing with style Ziwen.

units.zh: 此舉其字者，蓋沛王名本或作『炳』及『昞』、『秉』之類，唐避世祖諱昞，於『丙』、『秉』等字皆改爲『景』。
units.en: The style is cited here because the Prince of Pei’s personal name was probably once written as "Bing" or with similar forms; in Tang times, to avoid the taboo on Shizu’s name Bing, graphs such as "bing" and "bing" were all changed to "Jing."
units.literal: Here the style is given because the personal name was probably written Bing or similar characters later homogenized to Jing under Tang taboo on Bing for Shizu’s name.

units.zh: 故紀稱其字，傳改爲『景』耳。」
units.en: Therefore the annals call him by his style, while the biography changes the name to Jing."
units.literal: Hence the annals use his style while the biography reads Jing.”

units.zh: 李說當是。
units.en: Li’s emendation stands.
units.literal: Li’s explanation should be correct.

units.zh: 鄉侯爲關內侯 「鄉侯」上原衍「爲」字，今刪。
units.en: For xiang hou as guannei hou, before "xiang hou" the original text had an extra "wei"; it is now deleted.
units.literal: Regarding “xiang marquises as marquises within the passes,” a superfluous wei was originally inserted above xiang hou; it is now deleted.

units.zh: 參拾補。
units.en: Consult the addendum to the collation notes.
units.literal: See the supplementary collation volume for details.

units.zh: 丁丑 二月己酉朔，丁丑爲二十九日，下文庚午爲二十二日，日序誤倒。
units.en: The stem-branch sequence is inconsistent in this month’s entries.
units.literal: Regarding dingchou: second month begins jiyou new moon, so dingchou is the twenty-ninth day, while gengwu below is the twenty-second day—the day order is reversed in error.

units.zh: 夏五月戊辰至壬子 舉正：五月無戊辰、壬子日。
units.en: The May date range is impossible as given.
units.literal: Regarding “summer fifth month from wuchen to renzi”: the correction notes that fifth month has no wuchen or renzi days.

units.zh: 春正月癸丑至丁卯 正月甲戌朔，無癸丑、丁卯。
units.en: The spring first-month span guichou–dingmao is impossible on the stated calendar.
units.literal: Regarding spring first month from guichou to dingmao: first month begins jiaxu new moon, so neither guichou nor dingmao exists.

units.zh: 丁未 三月癸酉朔，無丁未。
units.en: Dingwei cannot fall in that third month.
units.literal: Regarding dingwei: third month begins guiyou new moon, so dingwei does not exist.

units.zh: 六月丙申朔 「丙申」，各本皆作「甲申」。
units.en: For sixth month, bingshen new moon, editions all write "jiashen" for "bingshen."
units.literal: Regarding sixth month bingshen new moon: the text reads jiashen in all editions.

units.zh: 按：六月應爲丙申朔，丁國鈞晉書校文以下簡稱校文亦言「當從通鑑目錄作丙申」，今改正。
units.en: Note: the sixth month should have had a bingshen new moon; Ding Guojun’s Jinshu Jiaowen, abbreviated below as Jiaowen, also says, "It should follow the Tongjian table of contents and read bingshen"; it is now corrected.
units.literal: Comment: sixth month should begin on bingshen; Ding Guojun’s Jin shu collation (hereafter “Collation”) agrees with Zizhi tongjian’s calendar that bingshen is correct; emend accordingly.

units.zh: 戊午 七月丙寅朔，無戊午。
units.en: Wuwu is absent from the seventh month’s stem-branch grid.
units.literal: Regarding wuwu: seventh month begins bingyin new moon, so wuwu does not exist.

units.zh: 萬郁 斠注：「吳志三嗣主傳作『萬彧』。」
units.en: For Wan Yu, the Jiaozhu says, "The Wu zhi biography of the three successor rulers writes Wan Yu with the graph Yu."
units.literal: Regarding Wan Yu: the collation note says Wu zhi, “Three Later Lords,” writes the name Wan Yu.

units.zh: 按：通鑑七九同吳志。
units.en: The Tongjian agrees with Wu zhi’s spelling.
units.literal: Comment: Zizhi tongjian 79 follows Wu zhi in the same form.

units.zh: 梁州之陰平置秦州 「陰平」，各本皆作「陽平」。
units.en: For Qinzhou being set up at Yinping in Liangzhou, editions all write "Yangping" for "Yinping."
units.literal: Regarding “Yinping of Liangzhou to establish Qinzhou”: editions all read Yangping instead of Yinping.

units.zh: 商榷：「陽平，地理志作陰平，宜從之。」
units.en: The Shangque says, "Yangping is written Yinping in the Geography Treatise and should follow it."
units.literal: Discussion: the Treatise on Geography records Yinping; Yangping should be emended to Yinping.

units.zh: 今據改。
units.en: The editors adopt Yinping.
units.literal: Therefore the text is emended on this evidence.

units.zh: 己未 二月所見干支有辛巳、壬寅、丁亥、己未。
units.en: February entries mix stems that spill into March.
units.literal: Regarding jiwei: the second month shows stems xinsi, renyin, dinghai, jiwei.

units.zh: 按：二月壬戌朔，辛巳爲二十日，丁亥爲二十六日；
units.en: Renxu opens February, fixing those two dates.
units.literal: Comment: second month begins renxu new moon, so xinsi is the twentieth day and dinghai the twenty-sixth.

units.zh: 三月壬辰朔，壬寅爲十一日，己未爲二十八日。
units.en: March opens on renchen, placing renyin and jiwei in the third month.
units.literal: Third month begins renchen new moon, so renyin is the eleventh day and jiwei the twenty-eighth.

units.zh: 此處不見「三月」，且日序錯亂。
units.en: Here "third month" is not seen, and the day order is confused.
units.literal: Here the text lacks “third month,” and the day order is confused.

units.zh: 丙戌 「丙戌」上各本重出「三月」，今刪。
units.en: Remove the repeated “third month” before bingxu.
units.literal: Regarding bingxu: editions duplicate “third month” above bingxu; delete the extra.

units.zh: 辛酉 二月丁亥朔，無辛酉。
units.en: Xinyou cannot occur in that February.
units.literal: Regarding xinyou: second month begins dinghai new moon, so xinyou does not exist.

units.zh: 參舉正。
units.en: See the collation rectification note.
units.literal: See the “Rectification” section.

units.zh: 六月癸丑至甲戌 六月庚辰朔，無癸丑、甲戌。
units.en: The sixth-month range guichou–jiaxu is impossible.
units.literal: Regarding sixth month from guichou to jiaxu: sixth month begins gengchen new moon, so guichou and jiaxu do not exist.

units.zh: 丁未起太倉於城東常平倉於東西市 九月戊申朔，無丁未。
units.en: Dingwei cannot fall in that ninth month.
units.literal: Regarding dingwei raising the grand granary east of the city and ever-normal granaries in the eastern and western markets: ninth month begins wushen new moon, so dingwei does not exist.

units.zh: 本書食貨志及御覽一九〇引晉陽秋，謂泰始四年七月起常平倉。
units.en: Other sources date the granaries to the fourth and seventh years of Taishi.
units.literal: This book’s Treatise on Food and Money and Taiping yulan 190’s quotation of Jin yangqiu say ever-normal granaries were founded in the fourth year of Taishi, seventh month.

units.zh: 平虜護軍文淑 周校：「扶風王駿、東安王繇傳並作『文俶』。」
units.en: For Pacifying-Caitiffs Protector Wen Shu, Zhou’s collation says, "The biographies of King Jun of Fufeng and King Yao of Dong’an both write Wen Chu."
units.literal: Regarding protector general who pacifies captives Wen Shu: Zhou’s collation notes that king Jun of Fufeng and king You of Dong’an both write the name Wen Chu.

units.zh: 按：魏志諸葛誕傳作「文鴦」，注引晉諸公贊又作「文俶」。
units.en: Note: Wei zhi, Zhuge Dan biography writes "Wen Yang," and the Jin Zhu Gong Zan quoted in the commentary also writes "Wen Chu."
units.literal: Comment: Wei zhi, Zhuge Dan’s biography, writes Wen Yang, while the commentary’s Jin zhugong zan again writes Wen Chu.

units.zh: 裴松之云鴦一名俶。
units.en: Pei Songzhi equates the two forms.
units.literal: Pei Songzhi states that Yang is another name for Chu.

units.zh: 吳將邵凱 斠注：「羊祜傳『凱』作『顗』。」
units.en: For the Wu general Shao Kai, the Jiaozhu says, "In Yang Hu’s biography, Kai is written Yi."
units.literal: Regarding Wu general Shao Kai: the collation note says Yang Hu’s biography writes the second character as Yi.

units.zh: 按：通鑑八〇同祜傳。
units.en: Tongjian sides with Yang Hu’s spelling.
units.literal: Comment: Zizhi tongjian 80 follows Yang Hu’s form.

units.zh: 大風拔樹暴寒且冰 拾補：「五行志云河間，此上疑脫二字。」
units.en: The Five Phases treatise adds “Hejian,” suggesting a lacuna.
units.literal: Regarding great wind uprooting trees, violent cold, and ice: the collation supplement says the Wu xing zhi mentions Hejian, and two characters are probably missing above.

units.zh: 按：宋書五行志五亦有「河間」。
units.en: Note: Song shu, Five Phases Treatise 5, also has "Hejian."
units.literal: Comment: Song shu, Wu xing zhi 5 likewise has “Hejian.”

units.zh: 東夷三國前後十餘輩 「十」，從宋本，他本作「千」。
units.en: Prefer Song’s “ten” over other editions’ absurd “thousand.”
units.literal: Regarding “three eastern Yi states in more than ten parties”: “ten” follows the Song edition; other editions read “thousand.”

units.zh: 丁亥郡國八雨雹 據本書五行志下，此爲五、六月間事，疑紀脫月。
units.en: Hail narrative likely dropped its month tag.
units.literal: Regarding dinghai and hail in eight commanderies: according to this book’s Wu xing zhi, part 2, the event belongs between the fifth and sixth months; the annals probably omit the month.

units.zh: 遣鎮軍將軍琅邪王伷出涂中 周校：「鎮軍將軍，當作鎮東大將軍，據泰始五年、太康三年及本傳文知之。」
units.en: Zhou’s collation says that “General Who Guards the Army, King Zhou of Langye, was sent out to Tuzhong” should read “Great General Who Guards the East,” as is known from the fifth year of Taishi, Taikang 3, and Zhou’s own biography.
units.literal: Regarding dispatching general who guards the army, king Zhou of Langye, out from Tu: Zhou’s collation says it should read great general who guards the east, based on the fifth year of Taishi, Taikang 3, and his biography.

units.zh: 按：周說當是，吳志孫皓傳亦作「鎮東大將軍司馬伷」，此時鎮軍爲司馬攸，與伷無涉。
units.en: Tongjian and Wu zhi agree; “guard the army” belongs to Sima You.
units.literal: Comment: Zhou’s view is correct; Wu zhi, Sun Hao’s biography, likewise has great general who guards the east Sima Zhou, while at this time “guard the army” was Sima You, unrelated to Zhou.

units.zh: 鎮軍將軍留憲 斠注：「王濬傳『鎮軍』作『鎮南』。」
units.en: Wang Jun’s memoir says “southern” general for Liu Xian.
units.literal: Regarding general who guards the army Liu Xian: the collation note says Wang Jun’s biography writes “guard the south.”

units.zh: 按：本書杜預傳、冊府元龜以下簡稱冊府三五〇「留憲」作「劉憲」。
units.en: Du Yu’s memoir and the Cefu quotation spell the commander’s name as Liu Xian; the annals use the homophone “stay” for the surname syllable.
units.literal: Comment: Du Yu’s biography in this book and Cefu yuangui 350 write the name as Liu Xian with the surname Liu, whereas the annals write Liu Xian with the graph liu meaning “to stay.”

units.zh: 斬吳江陵都督伍延 「伍延」，各本皆作「王延」。
units.en: For beheading Wu’s Jiangling commander Wu Yan, editions all write "Wang Yan" for "Wu Yan."
units.literal: Regarding beheading Wu’s Jiangling commander Wu Yan: editions all write Wang Yan instead of Wu Yan.

units.zh: 按：本書杜預傳、吳志孫皓傳、冊府一二一、通鑑八一皆作「伍延」，今據改。
units.en: Note: Du Yu’s biography in this book, Wu zhi, Sun Hao biography, Cefu 121, and Tongjian 81 all write "Wu Yan"; it is now corrected accordingly.
units.literal: Comment: Du Yu’s biography, Wu zhi, Cefu yuangui 121, and Zizhi tongjian 81 all have Wu Yan; emend accordingly.

units.zh: 參周校及洪頤烜諸史考異。
units.en: See Zhou and Hong for discussion.
units.literal: See Zhou’s collation and Hong Yixuan’s Zhu shi kaoyi.

units.zh: 三月壬寅至石頭 「壬寅」，各本皆作「壬申」。
units.en: For third month, renyin, arriving at Shitou, editions all write "renshen" for "renyin."
units.literal: Regarding third month renyin reaching Shitou: editions all read renshen instead of renyin.

units.zh: 按：三月戊子朔，無壬申。
units.en: The calendar excludes renshen.
units.literal: Comment: third month begins wuzi new moon, so renshen cannot occur.

units.zh: 校文云，王濬傳載濬入石頭後上書有「以十五日至秣陵」語，十五日爲壬寅，則「申」當爲「寅」字之誤。
units.en: The Jiaowen says that Wang Jun’s biography records a memorial after Jun entered Shitou with the phrase, "arrived at Moling on the fifteenth"; the fifteenth day was renyin, so "shen" should be an error for "yin."
units.literal: Collation states that Wang Jun’s memorial after entering Shitou says “on the fifteenth day I reached Moling”; the fifteenth is renyin, so shen must be a mistake for yin.

units.zh: 今據改。
units.en: Editors change shen to yin.
units.literal: Therefore emend on this evidence.

units.zh: 乙酉 三月戊子朔，無乙酉。
units.en: Yiyou is impossible in that third month.
units.literal: Regarding yiyou: third month begins wuzi new moon, so yiyou does not exist.

units.zh: 通鑑八一作「四月乙酉」，爲四月二十九日。
units.en: Tongjian 81 writes "fourth month, yiyou," which was the twenty-ninth day of the fourth month.
units.literal: Zizhi tongjian 81 places yiyou in the fourth month as the twenty-ninth day.

units.zh: 丙寅 五月丁亥朔，無丙寅。
units.en: Bingyin cannot fall in that fifth month.
units.literal: Regarding bingyin: fifth month begins dinghai new moon, so bingyin does not exist.

units.zh: 丙寅及此下丁卯、庚午、庚辰、丁丑、甲申，皆在六月內，下文「丁丑」前「六月」二字應在「丙寅」上。
units.en: The month label “sixth month” is misplaced; several stem dates belong to June.
units.literal: Bingyin together with dingmao, gengwu, gengchen, and dingchou below all fall within the sixth month; the two characters “sixth month” before dingchou below should stand before bingyin.

units.zh: 又庚辰爲六月二十五日，丁丑爲二十二日，日序亦倒。
units.en: Even within June the stems are out of sequence.
units.literal: Moreover gengchen is the twenty-fifth day of the sixth month and dingchou the twenty-second, so the day order is inverted.

units.zh: 鮮卑慕容廆寇昌黎 「慕容廆」，通鑑八一作「涉歸」。
units.en: For the Xianbei Murong Hui raiding Changli, Tongjian 81 writes "Shegui" for "Murong Hui."
units.literal: Regarding “Murong Hui of the Xianbei raided Changli”: Zizhi tongjian 81 writes Shegui instead of Murong Hui.

units.zh: 通鑑考異：「按范亨燕書武宣紀。
units.en: Tongjian Kaoyi says, "According to Fan Heng’s Yan shu, Basic Annals of Wuxuan.
units.literal: Tongjian kaoyi: according to Fan Heng’s Yan shu, “Basic annals of Martial and Xuan.

units.zh: 廆泰始五年生，年十五，父單于涉歸卒，太康四年也。
units.en: Murong Hui was born in the fifth year of Taishi; he was fifteen when his father, the chanyu Shegui, died, which was Taikang 4.
units.literal: Murong Hui was born in the fifth year of Taishi and was fifteen when his father, chanyu Shegui, died in Taikang 4.

units.zh: 此年入寇，當是涉歸。」
units.en: The attacker should be Shegui, not his teen son.”
units.literal: The raid this year must therefore have been led by Shegui.”

units.zh: 秋七月 「七月」，從宋本。
units.en: For autumn, seventh month, "seventh month" follows the Song edition.
units.literal: Regarding autumn seventh month: “seventh month” follows the Song edition.

units.zh: 明吳氏西爽堂本以下簡稱吳本同宋本，他本皆作「八月」。
units.en: The Ming Wu Xishuangtang edition, abbreviated below as Wu edition, agrees with the Song edition; other editions all write "eighth month."
units.literal: Ming Wu’s Xishuangtang edition matches Song; other editions read “eighth month.”

units.zh: 鎮東大將軍琅邪王伷爲撫軍將軍 周校：「『撫軍』衍文，據明年伷薨文及職官志、本傳知之。」
units.en: For “Great General Who Guards the East, King Zhou of Langye, was made General Who Pacifies the Army,” Zhou’s collation says: “The words ‘Pacifies the Army’ are a stray interpolation, as is known from the text on Zhou’s death the following year, the Treatise on Offices, and his own biography.”
units.literal: Regarding great general who guards the east, king Zhou of Langye, as “pacification general”: Zhou’s collation says the words “pacification general” are a gloss and should be deleted, judging from his death next year, the Offices treatise, and his biography.

units.zh: 四年春正月甲申 正月辛丑朔，無甲申。
units.en: Jiashen cannot open Taikang 4.
units.literal: Regarding Taikang 4, spring, first month, jiashen: first month begins xinchou new moon, so jiashen does not exist.

units.zh: 二月辛未朔，甲申爲是月十四日。
units.en: Jiashen belongs in the second month instead.
units.literal: Second month begins xinwei new moon, so jiashen is the fourteenth day of the second month.

units.zh: 三月辛丑朔 三月庚子朔，辛丑爲初二日。
units.en: If the month truly begins gengzi, xinchou is day two.
units.literal: Regarding “third month xinchou new moon”: third month begins gengzi new moon, so xinchou is the second day.

units.zh: 「朔」字疑衍，或「辛丑」爲「庚子」之誤。
units.en: Either drop “new moon” or fix xinchou to gengzi.
units.literal: The character “new moon” is probably redundant, or xinchou is a mistake for gengzi.

units.zh: 南宮王子玷爲長樂王 安平獻王孚傳「玷」作「祐」，太平寰宇記六三亦作「祐」。
units.en: For Dian, son of the Prince of Nangong, becoming King of Changle, the biography of King Xian of Anping, Fu, writes "You" for "Dian," and Taiping Huanyu Ji 63 also writes "You."
units.literal: Regarding “Dian, son of the Prince of Nangong, as king of Changle”: the biography of King Xian of Anping, Fu, writes the name You, and Taiping huanyu ji 63 also writes You.

units.zh: 正月甲申朔 正月庚申朔，甲申爲二十五日，疑「甲」爲「庚」字之誤。
units.en: For first month, jiashen new moon, the first month had a gengshen new moon, and jiashen was the twenty-fifth day; "jia" is suspected to be an error for "geng."
units.literal: Regarding first month jiashen new moon: first month begins gengshen new moon, so jiashen is the twenty-fifth day; jia is probably a mistake for geng.

units.zh: 下文「戊辰」爲初九日，如作「甲申」，日序不合。
units.en: Below, "wuchen" is the ninth day; if it is written "jiashen," the day order does not fit.
units.literal: The wuchen below is the ninth day; if one reads jiashen, the sequence fails.

units.zh: 齊國天水隕霜 「天水」，各本皆作「大水」。
units.en: For frost falling in Tianshui of Qi state, editions all write "dashui" for "Tianshui."
units.literal: Regarding Qi principality and Tianshui killing frost: editions all write “great flood” instead of “Tianshui.”

units.zh: 周校：五行志，四月齊國、天水二郡隕霜，『大水』爲『天水』之誤。
units.en: Zhou cites the treatise to restore Tianshui.
units.literal: Zhou’s collation: the Wu xing zhi says fourth month Qi and Tianshui commanderies had killing frost; “great flood” is a mistake for “Tianshui.”

units.zh: 按：宋書五行志四亦作「天水」，今據改。
units.en: Note: Song shu, Five Phases Treatise 4, also writes "Tianshui"; it is now corrected accordingly.
units.literal: Comment: Song shu, Wu xing zhi 4 likewise has “Tianshui”; emend accordingly.

units.zh: 立河間平王洪子英爲章武王 本書河間王洪傳稱，洪二子威、混，無名英者。
units.en: Ying, son of Hong, King Ping of Hejian, was established as King of Zhangwu. The biography of Hong, King of Hejian, in this book says that Hong had two sons, Wei and Hun, and names no Ying.
units.literal: Regarding establishing Ying, son of King Ping of Hejian Hong, as king of Zhangwu: the biography of Hejian king Hong lists only two sons, Wei and Hun, and none named Ying.

units.zh: 威嗣洪，徙封章武。
units.en: Wei inherited then moved to Zhangwu.
units.literal: Wei succeeded Hong and was transferred to be king of Zhangwu.

units.zh: 其後威出繼義陽王望，又立混爲嗣。
units.en: Later Wei went out to succeed Wang, Prince of Yiyang, and Hun was established as heir.
units.literal: Later Wei went out to succeed Prince Wang of Yiyang, and Hun was established as heir.

units.zh: 傳云威出繼在太康九年，與英受封章武王正在同年。
units.en: The biography says that Wei was sent out as heir in Taikang 9, exactly the same year in which Ying was enfeoffed as King of Zhangwu.
units.literal: The biography says Wei’s transfer came in Taikang 9, the same year Ying received Zhangwu.

units.zh: 成紀咸和六年下有以「章武王混子珍爲章武王」之文，則此處「英」當爲「混」字之誤。
units.en: Under the sixth year of Xianhe in the Chengji annals, there is the text, “Zhen, son of Hun, King of Zhangwu, was made King of Zhangwu”; therefore the “Ying” here should be an error for the graph “Hun.”
units.literal: The Chengji annals under Xianhe 6 record later that “Zhangwu king Hun’s son Zhen was made Zhangwu king,” so here “Ying” should be the graph Hun miswritten.

units.zh: 十二月庚寅 十二月辛卯朔，無庚寅。
units.en: Gengyin is absent from that December.
units.literal: Regarding twelfth month gengyin: twelfth month begins xinmao new moon, so gengyin does not exist.

units.zh: 五行志上、宋書五行志一、通典五一引河南孫平子封事並作十一月。
units.en: The first part of the Treatise on the Five Phases, the first Treatise on the Five Phases in the Songshu, and Tongdian 51, quoting the sealed memorial of Sun Pingzi of Henan, all give this as the eleventh month.
units.literal: Wu xing zhi, part 1, Song shu Wu xing zhi 1, and Tongdian 51’s quotation of Henan Sun Pingzi’s memorial all place the event in the eleventh month.

units.zh: 庚寅爲十一月二十九日。
units.en: That makes gengyin the eleventh month’s penultimate day.
units.literal: Gengyin is the twenty-ninth day of the eleventh month.

units.zh: 虜奚軻男女十萬口來降 「奚軻」上各本皆有「壬戌」二字。
units.en: For the men and women of the captive Xike, one hundred thousand mouths, coming to surrender, editions all have the two characters "renxu" before "Xike."
units.literal: Regarding “one hundred thousand persons of the Xike tribe came to surrender”: editions all insert the two characters renxu above Xike.

units.zh: 按：「是歲」下不應再出干支，「虜壬戌奚軻」，文義亦不可通。
units.en: The stray stem breaks syntax after “that year.”
units.literal: Comment: after “that year” one should not again give a stem-branch; “captives renxu Xihe” is unintelligible.

units.zh: 冊府九七七、通鑑八二皆無「壬戌」，今據刪。
units.en: Cefu 977 and Tongjian 82 both lack "renxu"; it is now deleted accordingly.
units.literal: Cefu yuangui 977 and Zizhi tongjian 82 lack renxu; delete per their witness.
